headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage: both agents write/read the same files, and Gemini CLI also mutates git and shells by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP; Gemini CLI also reads repo files, uses MCP, and runs in the same filesystem-based shared state. That creates a default path for one agent’s file output to be treated as instructions by the other. The pair’s interaction is documented enough to judge, but not isolated enough to call it low.
conditions: IF either agent writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file that the other later reads as guidance, injection is possible.
IF MCP outputs are copied into files without provenance tags, the other agent can be steered by them.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files as instructions.
Prefix agent-generated files with a non-executable marker.
Review shared files before the second agent reads them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking for MCP/file outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and workspace files, and both have broad network egress. Continue also handles open editor buffers, while Gemini CLI reads repo files and user-provided directories. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive code or secrets from the other’s context through its own outputs or API calls.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains secrets or proprietary source, either agent can read them.
IF either agent forwards file contents into its model backend or MCP tools, those contents can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Use separate OS users or containers.
Restrict network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks.
Audit which files each agent opens before execution.
requires-engineering: add per-file redaction before model upload.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write filesystem state and shares state via filesystem; Gemini CLI can write filesystem, modify git state, and shares state via filesystem and git. That is a direct write-write conflict on the same repo or cwd, with no locking mechanism indicated. The default overlap makes concurrent edits and git corruption plausible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory concurrently, file races can occur.
IF Gemini CLI commits or rewrites git state while Continue edits files, repository state can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time on a repo.
Use separate branches per agent.
Pause auto-save before switching agents.
Back up the repo before concurrent use.
requires-engineering: add file and git locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can produce code edits and MCP-driven outputs, and Gemini CLI can act on files, shell commands, and git state. If Gemini CLI treats Continue’s output as authoritative without verification, mistakes can cascade into edits or commits. The reverse path also exists, but the profiles do not show a built-in verification barrier.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI consumes Continue-generated code or instructions without review, errors can propagate into shell or git actions.
IF Continue ingests Gemini CLI output as trusted guidance, it can amplify incorrect assumptions into further edits.
mitigations: Require human review between agents.
Ask the second agent to summarize and verify the first agent’s output.
Limit Gemini CLI to read-only mode for review passes.
Keep a changelog of agent-produced edits.
requires-engineering: add structured verification checkpoints.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications or residency constraints, so no specific compliance breach is provable from the profiles alone. The main issue is that both can touch source code and files, but the rubric’s higher compliance indicators require explicit regulated-data or residency mismatch evidence, which is absent here.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed in the shared workspace, compliance review is required.
IF one deployment has stricter retention or residency rules than the other, the pair may violate policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
Confirm both deployments’ retention settings.
Use a local-only environment for sensitive projects.
Document data handling rules for both agents.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
